hypotheses.title: Parser error recovery is superlinear on deeply nested cascading syntax errors
hypotheses.issue: For N-deep nested inline record types where each nested field lacks a name (cascading syntax errors), parser error recovery takes ~O(N^2.3): N=20 1.43s, N=40 4.35s, N=80 14.3s. ~51% is in parser/error_handler.go recovery search (fixAndContinue -> seekInAlternativesPaths -> seekMatchInSubTree -> SeekMatch), ~21% in getCtxStackSnapshot, which copies the whole O(depth) context stack per explored alternative path, and ~30% GC (those copies plus traceRecovery closures that escape even with tracing off).

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generators for H1 candidates.
  gen.py recovery N  -> repro_recovery_N.bal : N-deep nested inline record types, each nested field
                        missing its name (syntax errors; parser error recovery cost grows ~N^2.3)
  gen.py defaults N  -> repro_defaults_N.bal : one function with N defaultable params, called N times
                        with one named arg (valid; cost is dominated by birgen, O(N^3))
"""
import sys
kind, n = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
if kind == "recovery":
    src = "type R " + "record { int a; " * n + "}" * n + ";\npublic function main() { }\n"
elif kind == "defaults":
    s = ["function f(" + ",".join(f"int p{i} = {i}" for i in range(n)) + ") returns int { return " + "+".join(f"p{i}" for i in range(n)) + "; }",
         "public function main() { int t = 0;"]
    s += [f"  t += f(p{i % n} = 1);" for i in range(n)]
    s.append("if t == 0 {} }")
    src = "\n".join(s) + "\n"
else:
    sys.exit("unknown kind")
open(f"repro_{kind}_{n}.bal", "w").write(src)
reproducer.command: python3 gen.py recovery 40 && go build -o bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -v ./bal run repro_recovery_40.bal

hypotheses.reason: Needs input with syntax errors, so `bal run` exits 1 and the benchmark tool (hyperfine and /usr/bin/time modes) cannot measure it; no valid-code reproducer. Possibly worth a look for language-server responsiveness. Out-of-scope side findings: birgen generateCallSite/snapshotIfNeeded is ~O(N^3) for N defaultable params called N times (N=200: 8s/4.5GB); 1000-deep nested else-less if panics in diagnostics with a negative startOffset (projects/package_compilation.go:245).

hypotheses.title: BDD op memo keyed by node pointer makes subtype checks against unions of N distinct error types O(2^N)
hypotheses.issue: semtypes BDD operations (bddUnionWithMemo/bddIntersectWithMemo/bddDiffWithMemo in semtypes/bdd_common_ops.go) memoize on bddOpMemoKey{B1 bdd, B2 bdd}: interface values compared by pointer identity. bddDiffInner with cmp>0 recurses twice, on diff(b1, union(b2.left, b2.middle)) and diff(b1, union(b2.right, b2.middle)). Every bddUnion/bddCreate result is a freshly allocated node, so structurally equal sub-BDDs reached by different paths never hit the memo, and the recursion branches 2-way per level of a union's middle chain. A union of N `distinct` error types (stdlib pattern: type Error distinct error<Detail>; type E_i distinct Error; type U E0|...|E_{N-1}) has one distinct-id atom per member, so `U u = error E0(...)` (stage 6 semantics/internal/analysis/constructors.go:validateErrorConstructor -> expressions.go:validateResolvedType -> semtypes.IsSubtype -> errorOps.Diff -> bddSubtypeDiff) costs O(2^N) time and memory: about 4x per 2 extra members, and N=22 takes 18.8s/3.06GB. Each node already has a hash-consed structural identity, canonicalKey() (bddKey, interned by internBddNodeKey when the node is built), which the memo ignores.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a stdlib-style distinct error hierarchy and a union of N members.
Usage: python3 gen.py N > repro.bal"""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 20
o = ["type Detail record { string code; };", "type Error distinct error<Detail>;"]
o += [f"type E{i} distinct Error;" for i in range(n)]
o.append("type U " + "|".join(f"E{i}" for i in range(n)) + ";")
o.append('public function main() { U u = error E0("m", code="x"); if u.message() != "m" { panic u; } }')
print("\n".join(o))
reproducer.command: python3 gen.py 18 > repro18.bal && ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> repro18.bal (or: go build -o bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -v ./bal run repro18.bal)

hypotheses.baseline: main: N=16 0.22s/80MB, N=18 0.83s/221MB, N=20 4.05s/783MB, N=22 18.8s/3.06GB. Profile at N=20: 66% cum under validateErrorConstructor->IsSubtype->bddDiffWithMemo (bddUnionWithMemo 38%, newBddNodeImpl 8%, internBddNodeKey 5%), ~33% GC.

hypotheses.fix_approach: Key the per-operation memo on the operands' structural keys instead of node identity: bddOpMemoKey{B1, B2 bddKey}, built from b1.canonicalKey()/b2.canonicalKey(), used in all three *WithMemo functions. This is sound because bddKey is hash-consed from {atom key (index, gen, rec), left, middle, right}; leaves have fixed keys (nothing=1, all=2) and interned keys start at 3, so equal keys mean equal structure. canonicalKey() is a precomputed field read, so the common path gets no extra cost, and the map key shrinks from two interfaces to two ints. The memos map operand pair to result only (no in-progress markers), so the change is safe. Possible extras not prototyped: share one memo through bddComplement/bddCreate, which call bddUnion with a fresh memo, or hash-cons nodes so pointer equality equals structural equality. make test passed.
